symptom: `call external action M.Client.NotThere`, or the right action name in another case (`dothing` for `DoThing`), passed `check -p` and `exec`; `mx check` reported CE7251 "Service 'M.Client' does not contain action 'dothing'." plus CE0117 on the output variable.
file: mdl/executor/validate_external_action_names.go ValidateExternalActionNames (MDL111), wired in validate_program.go; tests validate_external_action_names_test.go
cause: The flow builder's externalActionContract matches the action case-insensitively (strings.EqualFold) to type the result and the parameters, and the writer stores the name as typed, so a wrong-case name was typed correctly and written wrong; an absent name was simply written.
insight: **A lenient lookup in the builder is a strict one waiting to fail downstream.** The builder's EqualFold made a wrong-case action look resolved (its return type was found), which is exactly why nothing complained; Mendix compares the stored name exactly. The rule reads the contract stored on the project's consumed service (types.ParseEdmx over Metadata), and does not judge a service the script creates, alters or drops, whose contract is not the stored one. Needs `check -p`, so there is no no-project .fail fixture; proven end to end on a project with the contract imported (check -p and exec refuse NotThere and dothing, accept DoThing).
